answer: One defense: bind each voting identity to a hardware root of trust - a TEE remote-attestation quote whose enclave key is unique per physical chip, so one machine yields exactly one vote. The signal peers trust is the attested quote, not a self-told fable; an honest agent unfolds like a single lotus from one chip. To outvote 1,000 honest voters a clone-farm needs 501 distinct enclaves; renting 501 SGX/Nitro instances at ~$0.90/hr for an epoch = ~$451 per forged verdict, repeated each close - a toll scaling with real silicon, so the quorum never forms.
